sophia kim: Quick heads-up — on onboarding `kestrel-13b` (converted from Gemma -> Llama layout) I hit a weird embed-projection wobble after int4 quant. Tiny repro below, filing here before I dig deeper. :thinking:

kevin li: repro + logs pls? which conversion script and quant tool/version?

sophia kim: repro command I used:
```bash
python tools/convert_model.py 
  --src gemma-kestrel-13b/weights.bin 
  --dst kestrel_pt/ 
  --layout llama --preserve-vocab false
python tools/quantize.py --model kestrel_pt --bits 4 --scheme q4_0
```
Output: `max_embed_cosine_diff: 0.042` and local tests show top-1 token neighbours change for tokens around 49000-50270.

maria ramos: hmm two quick suspects: 1) conversion injected extra sentinel/added tokens into the middle of the vocab, 2) rotary/head-dim mismatch during weight reshape. Did you preserve `token_to_id` ordering or use a remap?

sophia kim: I passed `--preserve-vocab false` because upstream gemma tokenizer has `added_tokens` in the JSON. The conversion script appends them, but maybe the loader used by our runtime inserts them earlier.

jonah park: can you run a compare of the embedding projection matmul output for the same token ids on float32 vs converted-int4 (before softmax)? small script will show whether it's a rotate/shift or a per-row corruption. Also check KV cache slotting if kvcache index offset is coming from token id shift.

sophia kim: ran quick compare. snippet:
```python
# compare_embeds.py (very small)
left = load_weights('kestrel_pt/float32/emb_proj.npy')
right = load_weights('kestrel_pt/int4/emb_proj.npy')
cos = rowwise_cosine(left, right)
print('max_cosine_diff', cos.max())
# per-token diagnostic
for tid in [48995,49000,50010,50265]:
    print(tid, cos[tid])
```
output:
```
max_cosine_diff 0.042
48995 0.001
49000 0.41
50010 0.39
50265 0.40
```
so diffs spike for token ids >= 49000.

kevin li: that pattern screams vocab remap insertion. If added tokens were inserted at index 49000 by the runtime loader, emb rows would shift. Confirm tokenizer vocab file on the runtime side (not the converted model) — sometimes our tokenizer merges added tokens into middle when `added_tokens` has indices set.

maria ramos: also confirm rotary/base/freq table: if head-dim or num-heads changed during conversion we sometimes reshape the linear weights incorrectly leading to per-head swaps that look like a shifted token pattern. But your row diffs pointing to a contiguous block implies vocab insertion before weight packing.

sophia kim: checked runtime tokenizer: it has an extra sentinel token `<|sentinel_0|>` inserted at index 49000 (weird). The original gemma vocab had it appended at end (50270). So runtime is inserting into the middle.

jonah park: ah — conversion path: our `tokenizer_merger` step was running and applying `add_special_tokens` with `insert_at` semantics. We recently changed default to insert instead of append to keep some sequence of reserved indices. That explains it.

kevin li: quick mitigation: convert with explicit tokenmap that preserves original indices. i.e. `--tokenmap-preserve-order true` or pass a `token_index_map.json` that maps gemma indices -> runtime indices. Then re-pack weights without shifting rows.

sophia kim: patched conversion to include `--tokenmap-preserve-order true`. reran quantize. small compare now shows:
```
max_cosine_diff 0.0009
48995 0.0002
49000 0.0004
50010 0.0003
50265 0.0005
```

eval-bot: EVAL START — running quick zero-shot NLI and summarization smoke suite on `kestrel-13b-int4` (after preserve-order fix).

ci-bot: CI job started: `tests/onboard/kestrel-smoke` (build 4872).

eval-bot: EVAL DONE — NLI acc delta: -0.02% vs float32 baseline, Rouge-L on summarization delta: -0.03%. int4 quantization with preserved token indices looks sane.

maria ramos: great catch. We should add a conversion test that verifies a token-index invariance property: for all tokens in `tokenizer.added_tokens`, ensure mapping either appends or is accompanied by a weight-row-shift that we explicitly apply. Put it in `tests/onboard/tokenmap_invariance.py`.

jonah park: agreed. I'll open a PR to default `--tokenmap-preserve-order` for model families that expose `added_tokens` in the tokenizer JSON, plus a small warning message during conversion.

sophia kim: thanks all — iterating on docs and adding the regression test. Leaving the thread with the exact debug artifacts in `s3://redwood-onboard/kestrel/3187654321/` (embed diffs, tokenmaps, conversion logs). :thumbsup:
